"Build a 3D physics-based boxing game for mobile (touch controls) with desktop fallback. Target stack: [Unity / Unreal / Three.js + Rapier]. Prioritize a playable vertical slice first, then expand.

CORE FIGHT SIMULATION
- Physics-driven ragdoll/active-ragdoll hybrid: animation-driven movement, physics-driven impacts.
- Punch types: jab, cross, lead/rear hook, lead/rear uppercut, body shots, overhand, check hook, counter variations. Each has startup, active, recovery frames, and hip/shoulder rotation that affects power.
- Damage model based on impact force, glove contact point, punch angle, timing (counters hit harder), and target's guard/head position.
- Movement: footwork, pivots, clinches, ring cutoff, ducking, slipping, parrying, shoulder roll, blocking, bobbing and weaving.
- Stamina, momentum, balance, and chin/body durability stats that affect knockdowns, flash KOs, and accumulated damage.
- Referee AI: counts, breaks clinches, warns for low blows, stops fights (TKO).

ANATOMY AND DAMAGE
- Anatomically accurate skeleton, muscle groups, and facial structure (brow, cheekbones, nose, jaw, ribs, liver, solar plexus).
- Region-based damage: cuts (brow, cheek, lip), swelling, bruising, broken nose, bleeding progression over rounds.
- Realistic blood: drips, smears on gloves/canvas/shirts, localized wounds, staged intensity. Include a toggle to reduce or disable gore.
- Fatigue visuals: heavy breathing, dropped hands, slower footwork, sweat shaders.

CHARACTER CREATION AND CAREER
- Deep customization: face sculpting, body type, height, reach, stance (orthodox/southpaw), skin tone, hair, tattoos, scars, trunks, robes, gloves, mouthguard.
- Fighting style archetypes (swarmer, out-boxer, slugger, counter-puncher, boxer-puncher) with skill trees.
- Career mode: amateur to pro, training camps, sparring partners, stat progression, injuries, fatigue management, rankings, belts, sponsors, rivalries.
- Original fictional boxers inspired by real fighting styles and physiques (e.g., \"tall Cuban-style southpaw technician,\" \"Philly-style defensive counter-puncher,\" \"Mexican pressure body-puncher\"). Do not use real names, faces, or logos.

CUT MAN MINI-GAME (between rounds)
- Corner screen with trainer, cut man, and bucket.
- Touch-based tasks: apply pressure, swab, apply adrenaline/Vaseline, ice swelling, clean eyes, give water.
- Quality of treatment affects cut severity, swelling, and stamina recovery. Time-limited (60 seconds).

SPARRING MODE
- Headgear, bigger gloves, lower damage, focus on technique.
- Coach feedback, drills, punch accuracy stats, replay breakdown.

MULTIPLAYER
- Online 1v1 ranked and casual, rollback netcode or server-authoritative physics reconciliation.
- Matchmaking by skill tier, custom boxer sharing, spectator mode, rematches, leaderboards.

VENUES
- Photorealistic arenas: Vegas casino ballroom, Madison Square–style arena, UK football stadium, gritty small-hall fight, outdoor event, backyard gym.
- Dynamic crowds, lighting, ring-announcer, broadcast camera angles, entrance walks, post-fight interviews.

VISUALS AND AUDIO
- Realistic gear: leather gloves with creasing, wraps, trunks with elastic waistbands, mouthguards, shoes, headgear.
- Skin subsurface scattering, sweat, bruising shaders, motion-captured-style animation.
- Directional audio: punch impacts by region, crowd reactions, corner voices, referee.

MOBILE CONTROLS
- Left thumb: virtual joystick for movement.
- Right side: swipe-based punching (direction = punch type, e.g., swipe up for uppercut, arc for hook), tap for jab.
- Dedicated buttons: block, slip/dodge, clinch, special/counter.
- Gesture options: drag head to slip, two-finger hold for guard.
- Haptic feedback on hits, adjustable sensitivity, left-handed layout, controller support.

DELIVERABLES
1. Architecture overview and folder structure.
2. Phase 1 vertical slice: one ring, two boxers, punch system, damage, referee, mobile controls.
3. Then add: customization, career, cut man, sparring, venues, multiplayer.
4. Provide full, runnable code per phase with comments.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"
